findings.description: WH says the friend wanted to witness their worth instead of asking the professor to assess that worth confidentially.

contexts.japanese:
「……とある大富豪の遺品である蔵書が大量に競売に掛けられていて、
その一部に、民俗学的にも考古学的にも、あるいはオカルト的な意味でも極めて価値の高いものが含まれていると思われる、
その価値を内密に見て欲しいというのです」
contexts.japanesePC: 「えぇ、あれは忘れもしない。１９８７年４月のことです。私は友人から、ある奇妙な依頼を受けました。……とある大富豪の遺品である蔵書が大量に競売に掛けられていて、その一部に、民俗学的にも考古学的にも、あるいはオカルト的な意味でも極めて価値の高いものが含まれていると思われる、その価値を内密に見て欲しいというのです。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……とある大富豪の遺品である蔵書が大量に競売に掛けられていて、
その一部に、民俗学的にも考古学的にも、あるいはオカルト的な意味でも極めて価値の高いものが含まれていると思われる、
その価値を内密に見て欲しいというのです」
contexts.WH: "Yes, I will never forget that.  It happened in April of 1987.  I received a certain strange request from a friend.  ......There was a large collection of books, which were the former possessions of a very rich man and were being sold at auction, and it was thought that some of them might have been extremely valuable to the study of archeology and folklore, as well as in an occult sense, so this friend wanted to witness their worth confidentially."
contexts.MG:
...There was a large collection of books, the former possessions of a very rich man, that were being sold at auction,
and it was thought that some of them might've been extremely valuable to the study of archeology and folklore, as well as in an occult sense,
so this friend wanted to witness their worth confidentially."
contexts.UP:
"......A large collection of books, the former possessions of a very rich man, were being sold at auction,
and it was thought that some of them might have been extremely valuable from an archaeological and folkloristic perspective, as well as in an occult sense,
so this friend wanted me to take a private look at their value."
contexts.note: UP restores asking the professor to appraise privately.

findings.sourceReading: その価値を内密に見て欲しい reports the friend’s request that the speaker examine/appraise the books privately.
findings.alternative: Wanted to witness could broadly convey wanting to know the value, and later appraisal restores the professor’s role, but the English assigns the looking to the friend and loses the requested expert assessment.

findings.description: WH says the dealer possessed the documents after Eva had them sold at auction instead of receiving them with instructions to auction them.

contexts.japanese:
都内の大手古物商が、歴史的価値が高いと思われる大量の古文書を入手する。
これは、右代宮絵羽が競売に掛けるよう依頼して預けたものであった。
contexts.japanesePC: これは、右代宮絵羽が競売に掛けるよう依頼して預けたものであった。

都内の大手古物商が、歴史的価値が高いと思われる大量の古文書を入手する。

findings.description: WH says collectors could not satisfy their desire to hoard the books rather than that the books were valuable enough to make them want to hoard them for possessive satisfaction.

contexts.japanese:
そんな、好事家たちが死蔵して独占欲を満たしたくなるほどに価値ある蔵書が２０世紀末に大量に発見、
公開されたことは、全世界に大きな衝撃を与えた…。
contexts.japanesePC: そんな、好事家たちが死蔵して独占欲を満たしたくなるほどに価値ある蔵書が２０世紀末に大量に発見、公開されたことは、全世界に大きな衝撃を与えた…。
contexts.japanesePS3:
そんな、好事家たちが死蔵して独占欲を満たしたくなるほどに価値ある蔵書が２０世紀末に大量に発見、
公開されたことは、全世界に大きな衝撃を与えた…。
contexts.WH: Those books, which were so valuable that dilettantes just couldn't satisfy their desire to hoard them away, were discovered in large numbers at the end of the 20th century, and their release to the public had given the entire world a massive shock...
contexts.MG:
Those books, which were so valuable that enthusiasts could never satisfy their desire to hoard them away, were discovered in large numbers at the end of the 20th century,
and their release to the public had given the entire world a massive shock...
contexts.UP:
The discovery of that huge number of books at the end of the 20th century, books so valuable that dilettantes were filled with the desire to hoard them away,
and their subsequent release to the public, gave the entire world a massive shock...
contexts.note: UP restores books inciting possessive hoarding.

findings.sourceReading: 好事家たちが死蔵して独占欲を満たしたくなるほどに価値ある describes an inducement: their value makes collectors want to keep them hidden and satisfy the desire for exclusive possession. 満たしたくなる is wanting to satisfy, not inability to satisfy.
findings.alternative: Collectors can have insatiable acquisitive desires, but the source does not make that psychological claim; it explains why such valuable books would be withheld from public access.

findings.description: WH reduces the bottle’s sealing condition to the bare fact that it was sealed as a basis for the police judgment.

contexts.japanese:
「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、
事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。
contexts.japanesePC: 「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。　また双方の筆跡は一致しました。これにより、漁師の発見したノート片の信憑性が増すこととなりました。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「警察は現場の状況とボトルの封印状況から、捏造の可能性は低く、
事故直前の数日以内に投棄したものと判断したようです。
contexts.WH: "It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the fact that the bottle was sealed, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a fabrication was low and that it had been abandoned no earlier than a few days before the accident.  And the handwriting for both matched.  This caused the credibility of the scraps of paper discovered by the fisherman to rise.
contexts.MG:
"It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the fact that the bottle had been sealed,
the police had decided that its likelihood of being a fabrication was low and that it had been abandoned no earlier than a few days before the accident.
contexts.UP:
"It seems that, due to evidence from the surrounding area and the intact state of the bottle's seal, the police had decided that its likelihood of being a hoax was low,
and that it had been cast out no earlier than a few days before the accident.
contexts.note: UP restores intact state of bottle seal.

findings.sourceReading: 現場の状況とボトルの封印状況 are the circumstances at the scene and the condition/state of the bottle’s sealing. The source leaves the relevant observed condition unspecified rather than asserting that simple seal presence is the entire basis.
findings.alternative: Being sealed is one possible relevant condition and scene evidence remains, but the English selects that narrower observation instead of preserving the broader unspecified evidentiary detail.

findings.description: WH supplies attention as the motive in Ange’s speculation about the author of the witch accounts.

contexts.japanese: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.japanesePC: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……魔女幻想を生み出したい何者かの、愉快犯的犯行としか思えない。
contexts.WH: ......I can only imagine that someone who wanted to give rise to an illusion of a witch carried out this crime for attention.
contexts.MG: ...It seems to me that the only possible explanation...is that someone who wanted to give rise to an illusion of a witch carried out this crime for their own enjoyment.
contexts.UP: ......I can only imagine that this was a crime committed for pleasure, by someone who wanted to create an illusion of a witch.
contexts.note: Both restore pleasure motive rather than the inherited attention motive.

findings.sourceReading: 愉快犯的犯行 describes a crime committed for amusement or the thrill of doing it. Ange can only conceive of someone seeking to generate a witch illusion doing such a thing; no particular desire for attention is specified.
findings.alternative: Seeking attention can overlap with such thrill-seeking behavior, especially for a public hoax. That plausible motive is nevertheless narrower than the motive stated here and is not established by the preceding speculation about the bottles.

findings.description: Kasumi’s resentment at Ange adopting a name she had so strongly rejected becomes a claim that Ange had rejected it repeatedly.

contexts.japanese: ……あんなに名乗るのは嫌だと言ってた須磨寺の名を、気安く名乗ってくれちゃうなんて…」
contexts.japanesePC: 「………………いけない子ねぇ、縁寿ちゃんは。……そういう悪知恵、姉さんの血なのかしらねぇ。……あんなに名乗るのは嫌だと言ってた須磨寺の名を、気安く名乗ってくれちゃうなんて…。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……あんなに名乗るのは嫌だと言ってた須磨寺の名を、気安く名乗ってくれちゃうなんて…」
contexts.WH: "...............What a bad child, Ange-chan.  ......I wonder if that craftiness is from Nee-san's blood.  ......To think that she would casually take on the name Sumadera after saying she'd hate to call herself that so often...

findings.sourceReading: あんなに名乗るのは嫌だと言ってた emphasizes the degree of Ange’s professed aversion to using the Sumadera name. The barb contrasts that strong aversion with her now casually adopting it.
findings.alternative: Repeated objections could express strong aversion, and the English retains rejection and the irony of her current use. However, so often selects recurrence rather than the intensity expressed here; no frequency is specified.

findings.description: The Japanese compares the vessel’s importance for weakened Ange to bicycle training wheels, then escalates it to a chain. WH instead says it is important for her bike to have those parts.

contexts.japanese:
「………次に、依り代。
…今の縁寿には自転車の補助輪、…いえ、チェーンくらい大事」
contexts.japanesePC: 「………次に、依り代。…今の縁寿には自転車の補助輪、…いえ、チェーンくらい大事。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「………次に、依り代。
…今の縁寿には自転車の補助輪、…いえ、チェーンくらい大事」
contexts.WH: ".........Next is the vessel.  ...Right now, it's important for your bike to at least have training wheels, ...no, a chain."
contexts.MG:
"......Next is the vessel.
...Right now, it's important for your bike to at least have training wheels...no, a chain."
contexts.UP:
".........Next is the vessel.
...Right now, that's as important for you as a bicycle having training wheels—no, a chain."
contexts.note: UP restores bicycle analogy for the vessel rather than advising physical bicycle equipment.

findings.sourceReading: 次に、依り代 introduces the vessel as the topic. 今の縁寿には自転車の補助輪、…いえ、チェーンくらい大事 means that for Ange now it is as important as training wheels—no, as a bicycle chain. The revision intensifies the comparison from assistance to a basic operating necessity.
findings.alternative: A reader can reconstruct an analogy because bicycles otherwise have no role in the scene and vessel is introduced first. However, your bike and at least have replace the explicit degree comparison and its escalation with a literal possession-and-equipment claim.

findings.description: WH makes the stake the subject of the first upward movement, then describes Mammon’s stake rising again.

contexts.japanese:
私がかざす手を徐々に高め、頭より高く掲げると、
まるでそれに吸い寄せられるように、マモンの杭もまた、宙高く浮かび上がり、……徐々に震え始める。
contexts.japanesePC: 私がかざす手を徐々に高め、頭より高く掲げると、まるでそれに吸い寄せられるように、マモンの杭もまた、宙高く浮かび上がり、……徐々に震え始める。
contexts.japanesePS3:
私がかざす手を徐々に高め、頭より高く掲げると、
まるでそれに吸い寄せられるように、マモンの杭もまた、宙高く浮かび上がり、……徐々に震え始める。
contexts.WH: The stake I held out rose bit by bit, rising higher than my head, and as though it was being attracted upwards, Mammon's stake once again floated up high into the air, ......and gradually began to shake.
contexts.MG:
After I raised my hands bit by bit, lifting them higher than my head,

I slowly raised my hand, and as I brought it higher than my head,

findings.description: WH reverses the relation between summoning and rehabilitation in Maria’s caution and Ange’s answering challenge.

contexts.japanese:
マモンを呼び出せただけで、リハビリには十分だよ」
「あら、１人だけでリハビリになっちゃうの？
contexts.japanesePC:
「………縁寿。無理しないで。マモンを呼び出せただけで、リハビリには十分だよ。」
「あら、１人だけでリハビリになっちゃうの？　どうせ暇潰しよ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
マモンを呼び出せただけで、リハビリには十分だよ」
「あら、１人だけでリハビリになっちゃうの？
contexts.WH:
".........Ange.  Don't overdo it.  You'll need enough rehabilitation just from summoning Mammon."
"Oh, I'll need rehabilitation just from one?  Well, I'm just killing time anyways.
contexts.MG:
You'll need plenty of rehabilitation just from summoning Mammon."
"Oh, I'll need to rehabilitate after just one?
contexts.UP:
Just being able to summon Mammon is more than enough rehabilitation."
"Oh, I'm rehabilitated after just one?
contexts.note: UP restores summoning as sufficient rehabilitation rather than requiring rehabilitation afterward.

findings.sourceReading: マモンを呼び出せただけで、リハビリには十分 says merely having managed to summon Mammon is sufficient for rehabilitation: it is enough practice toward regaining her ability. Ange replies that just one already counts as rehabilitation (１人だけでリハビリになっちゃうの), then elects to keep going as a pastime.
findings.alternative: Summoning is exhausting in both versions, so needing recovery afterward is plausible and later warnings about fatigue remain accurate. However, that is a different causal relation: the source calls the summons itself rehabilitation, not a cause requiring rehabilitation afterward.

findings.description: Satan’s reproach gains an accusation that the sisters are not appreciative of another chance to serve.

contexts.japanese: 再びお役に立てる機会を賜るどころか、新しい主人の負担になるなんて、そんなの家具の名折れッ！！
contexts.japanesePC: 「私たちはベアトリーチェさまより休むことを許された、役目を終えた家具なのよ！　再びお役に立てる機会を賜るどころか、新しい主人の負担になるなんて、そんなの家具の名折れッ！！　早く姿を消しなさいッ！！」
contexts.japanesePS3: 再びお役に立てる機会を賜るどころか、新しい主人の負担になるなんて、そんなの家具の名折れッ！！
contexts.WH: "We are furniture who have been granted rest by Beatrice, and whose duty has been finished!  Not only are you not honored at being given another chance to be of some use, but you're putting a burden on our new master, you disgrace to furniture!!  Erase yourselves right away!!"
contexts.MG: Not only are you not honored at being given another chance to be of some use, but you're putting a burden on our new master, you disgrace to all furniture!!
contexts.UP: Not content to be graced with the opportunity to once again be of some use, you are putting a burden on your new master—this is a DISGRACE to furniture!!
contexts.note: Both retain an accusation of dissatisfaction instead of contrast between usefulness and burden.

findings.sourceReading: 再びお役に立てる機会を賜るどころか、新しい主人の負担になる contrasts being granted another opportunity to be useful with instead becoming a burden to the new master. The disgrace is their negative effect on Ange rather than insufficient gratitude for an opportunity.
findings.alternative: Not honored at being given another chance could be read as a contrast between receiving an honor and becoming a burden. In ordinary English its at construction instead describes their response to the opportunity, especially followed by but you’re putting a burden, adding a distinct reproach absent from the Japanese.
